stories.title: Storm Boelo: Orange wind warning in place for Donegal
stories.summary: Storm Boelo has brought severe wind and rain to the south, southwest and north of Ireland while a Status Orange wind alert remains in place for Donegal. The alert, which has been in place since 2pm yesterday, is valid until 9am. Counties Leitrim, Galway, Mayo and Sligo were all previously under a Status Orange wind warning as well, but are now under a Status Yellow warning. As of 3am, there were more than 20,000 homes and businesses without power, according to the ESB's PowerCheck service. Severe winds are impacting northern and western counties as the storm tracks to the north of the country. Met Éireann has warned of potential impacts including damage to already weakened structures, damage to power lines and power outages, large coastal waves and the displacement of loose objects.

stories.title: Minister says meeting with solicitors likely next week
stories.summary: The Minister for Justice has confirmed that he has "engaged" with solicitors and that a meeting is likely next week. Speaking at the launch of One In Four's annual report, Jim O’Callaghan said letters had been exchanged. A majority of solicitors working in criminal legal aid across the country have been in dispute with Mr O'Callaghan since a new €520 flat-fee payment for legal aid cases was introduced in July. Mr O’Callaghan insists that legal aid continues to be granted by the courts; solicitors continue to provide representation, and defendants continue to receive legal services throughout the State. This week, the minister said he would meet the Law Society of Ireland regarding the dispute. In a letter to President of the Law Society of Ireland Rosemarie Loftus, Mr O'Callaghan said he had instructed his officials to "organise a meeting in the coming days to hear your viewpoint and specific concerns".

stories.title: Euro zone growth slows to 4-month low amid French turmoil
stories.summary: Growth across the euro zone's private sector slowed to its weakest pace in four months in October, driven by an energy-driven rise in costs and a renewed contraction in France amid political and financial pressures, a survey showed today. The S&P global flash euro zone Composite PMI ⁠Output Index fell to 51.9 in October from September's 53.1, its lowest reading since June and lower than all forecasts in a Reuters poll which had predicted a modest dip to 52.7. "Key to the broader slowdown is the further escalation of inflationary pressures seen during the month," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Input costs are rising sharply again, the rate of increase surging in manufacturing on the back of higher energy prices, causing firms to push selling prices higher in order to protect margins," he said. Input costs accelerated for the second consecutive month linked to higher energy, fuel and transport costs in part due to the Middle ‌East war. Despite this, firms raised their ⁠selling prices at a slower pace than in September, suggesting some margin compression. "Higher interest rates are also starting to take a toll, dampening demand, and the picture of sustained growth and stubbornly elevated inflation from the October flash PMI will likely add to further speculation of more aggressive policy tightening from the ECB," Williamson added.

stories.title: Israel demolishes homes in West Bank after fatal attack
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Israel would lock down Hebron in the West Bank, go house to house and demolish homes after the Israeli military ⁠said Palestinian attackers killed two soldiers at a military checkpoint near the city. The Israeli military said it had killed two attackers, and another three soldiers had been lightly wounded in the attack. In a visit to Hebron after the attack, Mr Netanyahu said Israeli forces would enter the neighbourhood of the attackers and displace its residents. "We will evacuate the residents, we will go from house to house, we will also seize the weapons there, and all the terrorist infrastructure will be dealt with and destroyed," Netanyahu said, according to his office. "The defence minister and I are considering a very extensive IDF (army) operation in Judea and Samaria, such as has not been carried out since the Six Day War," Mr Netanyahu added, referring to the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. "The IDF is ready to execute it and we will set the timing, but it is on the way."

stories.title: Carrick trusts United to be a 'different team' v Cherries
stories.summary: Under-fire Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that Manchester United are unmanageable and trusts the players to bounce back from their Como calamity with a vital win against Bournemouth. Ruben Amorim's successor not only steadied the ship after his January arrival but steered the club to a third-place finish, although the former midfielder now looks to be heading into the rocks. United have recorded just two victories from their 11 matches this season, with Wednesday’s 4-1 humbling at the hands of Champions League upstarts Como extending their winless run to seventh match. It was quite the slump having talked up their training performance ahead of earning a purposeful point at Leeds last Sunday that he felt marked a "fresh start". Asked if he can trust the players to deliver against Bournemouth at Old Trafford given the last week, under-pressure Carrick said: "I definitely trust them, yeah, 100% I trust them. "It wasn’t a very good night at all for so many reasons. We all know that. I think that’s pretty obvious.

stories.title: McEntee to be named next Longford manager
stories.summary: Former Meath and Antrim manager Andy McEntee will be the new manager of Longford, pending ratification. The last vacant intercounty football position to be filled, McEntee will replace the outgoing Mike Solan, who has since joined Offaly, on a three-year term. McEntee recently interviewed for the Monaghan job having served as coach under Gabriel Bannigan last season, but lost out to namesake John McEntee. "Longford GAA Chairperson Derek Fahy welcomed Andy's nomination for the Senior Football Manager position and expressed his excitement for the future of the Senior Football Team," the Leinster county said. "He also expressed the hope that all clubs, members, supporters and players will give their full support to the new management team." McEntee guided Ballyboden, St Enda's to an All-Ireland Club title before going on to manage Meath, who he took to two Leinster finals.

stories.title: Jackson brace ends Man City's winning start to the season
stories.summary: Manchester City suffered defeat for the first time in the Premier League this season after Nicolas Jackson's double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park. Unai Emery’s side continued their turnaround in form after a slow start to the campaign and picked up a fourth straight win across all competitions, and their first league victory at home this season. Manchester City do not enjoy visiting Villa Park and have now lost their last four league games there, while Enzo Maresca saw his 100 per cent league start as City boss vanish. Another tough afternoon in the west Midlands started when Marc Guehi’s mistake allowed Jackson to give Villa an early lead. Villa had keeper Zion Suzuki to thank for making several vital saves, and Iliman Ndiaye crashed an effort off the post as Villa held strong to take the lead into the break. Erling Haaland grabbed his ninth league goal of the season to get City level but Jackson buried his second of the afternoon – his fourth of the season – on the hour mark to hand Villa the points.

stories.title: Ulster fall short in battling bid to beat Bulls
stories.summary: Ulster fell short as they were beaten 34-26 by the Bulls despite a superb fightback in their United Rugby Championship clash in Pretoria. The South African side raced into a 21-0 lead with two tries from former Ulster forward Marcell Coetzee either side of an effort from Elrigh Louw. Ulster replied on the stroke of half-time through Chay Mullins and David McCann reduced the arrears further after the restart. Coetzee was then sin-binned to give Ulster further encouragement but a Handre Pollard penalty checked their momentum. Mullins' second try put the Irish side within striking distance but Johan Grobbelaar crossed from close range to all but make the game safe. Ulster were given late hope when Stuart McCloskey forced his way over but Curwin Bosch’s last-minute penalty sealed the home side’s victory.

stories.title: Wexford Festival Opera - watch The Gambler by Sergei Prokofiev
stories.summary: We proudly present a live presentation from this year's Wexford Festival Opera - The Gambler by Sergei Prokofiev, with a libretto by the composer after Fyodor Dostoevsky. With its jagged, modernist score, The Gambler offers a chillingly relevant look at the price of desire. Place your bets on a night of operatic intensity and join us for this rare, visceral revival. Written in 1917 during the First World War when the composer was 26 years old and still considered to be in his enfant terrible phase, the opera was not performed until 1929. Based on Fyodor Dostoevsky’s 1866 novella, in this new production – marking the Wexford debuts of director Ivan Popovski and conductor Valentin Uryupin – nervous obsession spirals into self-destruction. Set in 1865 in the fictional German spa town of Roulettenburg, everything is deliberately artificial. The opera follows the protagonist, Alexei, a young tutor, as he spirals into gambling debt while being obsessed with his employer’s stepdaughter, Polina. In the final act, the casino itself emerges as the central character, controlling the destiny of those consumed by their passion for the roulette wheel, like moths to a flame. Prokofiev intended the work as a reaction against Romantic lyricism, instead preferring to create ‘an opera in the declamatory style’, closer in technique to the stageworks of Dargomyzhsky and Mussorgsky which set musical prose in natural speech rhythms. Find out more about this year's Wexford Festival Opera programme here

stories.title: Sinéad O'Shea: 'You want things to be unpredictable'
stories.summary: What happens when a man born into one of America's wealthiest families uses his inheritance to support movements that oppose capitalism? Irish filmmaker Sinéad O’Shea explores that question in her new documentary, All About the Money, which follows American heir Fergie Chambers and his efforts to fund political movements aligned with his communist beliefs. "As a documentary-maker, that is exactly what you want. You want things to be unpredictable," she said. "I suppose the reason why I was so interested in the first place was that I felt like it was such a potent situation." O'Shea said there were aspects of Chambers’ character that she appreciated, particularly his willingness to speak about economic inequality. stories.title: Embracing the history, flavours, and spectacular views of Türkiye
stories.summary: Tara Povey experiences the crystal-clear waters, ancient ruins and delicious flavours of Türkiye. Turkey officially became Türkiye in 2022, and I didn't even notice. Despite Istanbul sitting on my travel bucket list for years, I’d never visited. I knew the trope of people going to Türkiye with receding hairlines or dodgy teeth and coming back looking like reality TV stars, but that’s as far as my knowledge went. Then, one day, after some dramatic romantic ups and downs that you may have read about, I met a kind, handsome Turkish man and suddenly I was learning about the Ottoman Empire, and how Türkiye sent aid to Ireland during the Famine. At the end of September we visited Türkiye together for the first time. We both knew my melanin-deprived skin would be no match for the Turkish heat during peak summer when temperatures reach up to 40°C. We flew direct from Dublin to Antalya with Sun Express, picked up our rental car and set off to explore the turquoise coast. Konyaalti is a stunning 7km stretch of pebbly beach with crystal-clear water and the Taurus mountains acting as a dramatic backdrop. We stayed in an apartment in Konyaalti just a few minutes' walk from the beach.

stories.title: Over 22,000 taking part in 45th Dublin Marathon
stories.summary: The 45th Irish Life Dublin Marathon is taking place today, with thousands of runners taking part and many thousands of supporters expected to line the route through the city centre and suburban areas. There are a number of road closures, and diversions are in place across the capital. There will be more than 22,000 people running and jogging including elite athletes, wheelchair participants and charity fundraisers. The organisers said more than €5 million has been raised so far. The event gets under way just after 8am, with the Dublin Lord Mayor Daryl Barron's Medal presentation. A woman from Cavan, who has completed more than 600 marathons and continues to run while undergoing treatment for an incurable cancer, will receive the medal at the start line, which is on Leeson Street.

A post-mortem examination is due to be carried out by Assistant State Pathologist Dr Margaret Bolster. Gardaí have said that the examination will determine the course of the investigation but that it has been allocated the resources of a murder investigation. A senior investigating officer has been appointed and an incident room has been established at Macroom Garda Station.

stories.title: No measure can ease pain of scoliosis failures - minister
stories.summary: The Minister for Health has acknowledged that no measures the Government may introduce will alleviate the pain endured by those affected by failures in spina bifida and scoliosis services. She told the Dáil that stakeholders will be consulted by her officials, who will work with the Attorney General to draft terms of reference for a commission of inquiry. The minister was speaking during Statements on Children's Health Ireland (CHI), which was also attended in the visitors' gallery by some of those who have been advocating for action on the matter. Ms Carroll MacNeill said that she received the final scoping report on 9 September, and expressed her gratitude to Remy Farrell SC for his efforts to "capture the pain" and "very real frustration" of those affected. She noted that a commission of investigation, as recommended by Mr Farrell, allows for greater flexibility than a tribunal, including private hearings. She noted that witnesses can request whether to have their testimony heard in public or private.

stories.title: Lidl to invest €420m across Munster, creating 500 jobs
stories.summary: Lidl has today announced a €420m investment across Munster, which the supermarket group said will create more than 500 permanent jobs. €306m of the investment is earmarked for Co Cork, the company added. At the centre of the programme is Lidl's new €200m regional distribution centre at Little Island in Cork, alongside plans for 14 new stores across Munster and the redevelopment of 10 existing locations. As well as creating 500 jobs, including 250 in Cork, the company said the investment will also support more than 4,500 construction jobs across the 25 developments. Lidl currently employs more than 1,300 people across Munster and once the new investment is delivered, its permanent workforce in the region is expected to exceed 1,800. The €420m regional programme represents a significant part of Lidl's wider €600m five-year investment programme in Ireland, through which the retailer intends to open up to 35 additional stores around the country.

stories.title: Shooting near Paris a 'racist terrorist attack' - Macron
stories.summary: A gunman firing from his car killed one person and wounded five - including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times - near Paris, in what the French presidency condemned as a "racist terrorist attack". French President Emmanuel Macron visited the working-class town of Trappes southwest of Paris, where a gunman opened fire earlier in the day in an attack suspected of having targeted people of foreign origin. This was a "racist, terrorist attack", said the Elysee presidential palace. Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh said the man was "firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath" as he drove through Trappes and neighbouring La Verriere. Most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds and prosecutors are investigating whether the acts targeted the "real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion" of the victims. The 12-year-old girl shot eight times was "seriously wounded" but in a stable condition, the mayor of La Verriere, Nicolas Dainville, said.

stories.title: McMillan: 'Powers that be' to look at foul play incident
stories.summary: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan said "the powers that be" will decide on the outcome of an allegation of serious foul play, after his side's 24-18 defeat to Leinster at Aviva Stadium. Munster's injury-hit squad felt the full force of Leinster's internationals in the second half of their interpro, as McMillan's side saw their 13-0 lead wiped out by four Leinster tries. There was a major flashpoint late in the first half, when Munster's Gavin Coombes alleged he had been grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck. Referee Andrew Brace stopped play during the 39th minute and spent some time speaking to his TMO, who searched for footage of the alleged incident to no avail. While the officials weren't able to identify the incident during the game, it may still be referred to the citing commissioner. "It's one of those things that we leave in the hands of the powers that be," Munster head coach McMillan said.

stories.title: Downey the hero as Blues clinch dramatic Louth success
stories.summary: All-Star nominated Ciarán Downey stood up at the death to extend Newtown Blues' advantage on the Louth senior roll of honour with a two-pointer for the ages. In additional time, with his side trailing by one, Downey composed himself deep in the pocket to fire over the winner and break St. Mochta's hearts, notch title number 24 in the process. Mochta's had led the entire second half and looked to secure their first ever Joe Ward Cup but could not hold on. It was St Mochta's who had struck late in the drawn game with Declan Byrne kicking a stunning effort to force a second outing, but his first effort into the goal where he kicked 0-08 last week was wayward as the wind played a part. Then some atonement for two Blues men who were off colour the week before. All-Star nominee Downey clipped over after corner-forward Conor Moore opened the scoring for the Newfoundwell outfit. Mochta’s Gerry Garland levelled with a beautiful swirling effort from outside the boot as two evenly matched sides went level four times in total in the opening half.

stories.title: Infantino confident 'vast majority' of nations behind him
stories.summary: Gianni Infantino believes he has the support of the "vast, vast majority" of footballing nations as he seeks re-election as head of the game's world governing body. The Swiss has faced widespread calls to resign as president of FIFA since hatching plans to sell off a stake in the World Cup earlier this year. UEFA and CONCACAF, the bodies responsible the game in the European and North and Central American and Caribbean regions, were at the forefront of those demands but Infantino has withstood the pressure. He intends to stand for a fourth term as president at the next FIFA election in March and appears confident of having the required backing. Infantino told BBC Sport: "Well you know I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world. "I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view.

stories.title: Cullen still driven by 'amazing' Leinster-Munster rivalry
stories.summary: We're now deep into the "last time you will ever..." conversations with Leo Cullen on his farewell season. Not counting his days playing underage and schools Interpros, this evening's meeting at Aviva Stadium will be roughly the 60th clash of Leinster and Munster in which Cullen has either been a Leinster player, assistant coach or head coach. To put that in context, he's been a stakeholder in just over half of the games between the sides. There have been so many over the years that he struggles with the details of his first. He remembers it was "one of those Dooradoyle ones", with around 500 people well spread around the Limerick ground. A look through the archives suggests it might have been in 1998, where a 20-year-old Cullen would have been an unused sub behind Pat Holden and Gabriel Fulcher. The Leinster-Munster rivalry blossomed into one of rugby's biggest club fixtures in the nearly three decades since, and while there will still be one more Christmas Thomond Park visit for the departing Leinster coach, this evening could be his last time hosting the province in this fixture, barring a play-off draw.

stories.title: They did not go quietly - inside Ireland's last witch trial
stories.summary: It’s May 2026 and we are driving on a sunny weekday afternoon to the Islandmagee Peninsula, twenty miles north of Belfast. As the waters of Larne Lough, the body of water which separates Islandmagee from the mainland, comes into view the question arises, what do we believe really happened here on this remote spit of land back in 1711? The history books tell us that a young Presbyterian woman named Mary Dunbar was showing all the signs of demonic possession. Over a period of days, she named eight local women as witches, claiming they were responsible for her torment. The people of Islandmagee, at that time mostly Presbyterians of Scottish descent, believed Mary's accusations and the eight women were arrested, put on trial and found guilty. They are on record as fiercely protesting their innocence in court. Today the peninsula is a tourist attraction for visitors to the Gobbins, a cliff walkway suspended over the Irish Sea. Yet, there are traces of its past written into the landscape; stone built cottages clinging to hillsides, churches dating back to the 1500s, and a landmark steeped in folklore: the Witches’ Rocking Stone, a boulder overlooking Brown’s Bay.

stories.title: Oscar favourite Wildwood works on many levels, say stars
stories.summary: Peyton Elizabeth Lee and Jacob Tremblay have seen the just-released fantasy hailed as a landmark in animated filmmaking as studio LAIKA (Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls) and director Travis Knight champion stop-motion animation with their finest two hours to date. Wildwood tells the story of bolshy teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee - Andi Mack, Doogie Kameāloha, M.D.) and her bumbling pal Curtis (Jacob Tremblay - Room, Wonder) as they desperately search for Prue's baby brother - taken by a murder of crows and brought deep into the no-go lands that surround their Portland home. It mixes action and humour with themes of loss and belonging as Prue realises everyone needs some help from time to time while Curtis discovers he is stronger than he thinks. "I think there's a lot of mature themes to the film. So, this is the first film [from LAIKA] with a PG-13 rating, so that means a lot. But I think this definitely is a film a lot of people can enjoy." "The story works on many different levels that I think different people of different ages can relate to," continued co-star Lee. "The animation medium is so special because I think it allows you to connect with young people and tell stories that have darker thematic elements while it still feeling exciting and magical and fun.

stories.title: 15 of the best coffee shops in Ireland
stories.summary: Ireland's coffee scene is booming and winning acclaim on a global scale. Here, food and travel content creator Éadaoin Fitzmaurice shares her pick of the top 15 coffee shops around Ireland, so you not only have new places to visit, but delicious drinks waiting for you there. There's nothing quite like arriving in a new town or county during a staycation and tracking down the best coffee around - a place that will become a daily ritual for the duration of your stay. Grá Linn, located in the coastal village of Fethard-on-Sea, has become a gathering place for locals, weekend wanderers and those tracing the quieter corners of Wexford. Here you’ll find a speciality coffee culture with genuine small-town warmth, as well as great seasonal brunch dishes and pastries. Large windows frame the rhythm of village life outside, while inside the focus is on quality ingredients and thoughtful service. Whether you're fuelling up before exploring the Hook Peninsula, or returning from a sea swim at Baginbun Beach, Grá Linn is the perfect stop. Hey Darling has brought a distinctly modern energy to Kildare's coffee scene. With three branches across Sallins, Naas and Kill, this stylish coffee shop blends excellent coffee with a sharp eye for design, creating a space that feels as considered as the drinks being served.

stories.title: Nearly 1,000 people arrested during protests in France
stories.summary: Nearly 1,000 people were arrested during protests in France yesterday, as clashes erupted while protesters took to the streets in a number of cities. Police carried out the arrests as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. It comes a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order. Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes yesterday. Two people were "seriously" injured, Mr Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case. Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.

stories.title: Glenstal Abbey boarding school to close within two years
stories.summary: Glenstal Abbey, a well-known private school in Murroe, Co Limerick, is to shut down within the next two years. Annual fees at the school range from €14,950 for day pupils up to €24,000 for full boarding, according to the school's website. In a statement this evening, the trustees of Glenstal Abbey said the school will close no later than August 2028 and that the decision to do so was "not made suddenly, nor has it been made lightly". The trustees said that the abbey has "wrestled with the future of the school for many years" and that the demand for boarding education "has declined over time, while the cost of operating a small boarding school and providing the quality of education, care and facilities expected of Glenstal has continued to rise". They said that a detailed external assessment of the school stated "the kind of school we have here at Glenstal is not sustainable into the future". "We are particularly saddened that this decision will come as a considerable shock to many families," they said.

stories.title: Russian embassy criticises McEntee over Dáil statement
stories.summary: The Minister for Foreign Affairs and Defence has been accused of making "reprehensible and misleading" comments in the Dáil about Russia's role in the UN Security Council and its approach to UN peacekeeping missions. The Russian Embassy in Ireland took issue with Helen McEntee's statement this week that the current "Triple Lock" legislation allows Russia, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, "to have a say over which peacekeeping missions we can send our troops to". In a statement, the embassy said: "Contrary to her assertions, the UN Security Council does not vote on what countries take part in a peacekeeping mission - its composition is agreed in the course of multilateral consultations conducted by the UN Secretariat and the interested UN member-countries." It added: "The allegations by Minister McEntee are reprehensible and misleading, grossly distorting the substance and the meaning of procedures provided by the UN Charter." The Russian Embassy also took issue with her remarks that Russia is "attacking European member-states, including Germany, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Poland". "The Minister's speculations over Russia's 'attacks' on the EU countries are totally baseless, dangerously provocative and unacceptable," the statement said.

stories.title: Mortgage drawdowns by FTB hit highest level since 2008
stories.summary: Mortgage drawdowns by first-time buyers are at the highest level since 2008, according to the mortgage drawdowns figures released by the Banking and Payment Federation Ireland. A total of 14,217 mortgages to the value of almost €4.6 billion were drawn down by borrowers in the months of July, August and September. This is a 13% increase in volume compared to the same period last year. Most of this activity was driven by first-time buyers - with 8,164 mortgages they accounted for 60% of all drawdowns in the third quarter. "Our latest figures show continued momentum across the mortgage market, with growth in drawdowns across every customer segment during the third quarter of 2026," said Brian Hayes, chief executive at BPFI. Remortgaging and switching activities saw a sharp rise as well.

stories.title: Maine race close as Trump ends some Canadian tariffs
stories.summary: With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight re-election battle, President Donald Trump signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could benefit companies from the northern state. The Republican president's hefty tariffs on Canada have caused friction with the US neighbour to the north while creating problems for American businesses in Maine and other states that rely on certain Canadian goods. With the 3 November US midterm elections looming and Republicans fighting to retain control of both houses of Congress, Senator Susan Collins had urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting companies and farmers in Maine, a state that borders Canada. Mr Trump's order exempted plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, and packing crates and boxes, as well as fresh and dried seaweed, the White House said. The changes take effect on 30 October, four days before the election. Mr Trump added a number of Canadian products to the 50% tariff list to offset the tariff relief provided in his order, including carpets, paints, waste, shampoos, cocoa powder, wooden coffins, ice cream sticks, air-conditioning machines, chest freezers, archery equipment and canoes.

stories.title: Power shares the lead heading into Sunday in Bermuda
stories.summary: Ireland's Seamus Power will enter the final round's action at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship in a share for the lead after carding another under-par round on Saturday. Power is tied at the top with Austin Smotherman, with the pair sitting on 16 under par, two clear of the chasing pack. Following a sensational Friday at the Port Royal Golf Club, when he fired a seven-under 64, Power made an ideal start. The Waterford man birdied the par-four first hole and the par-three third to get to 14 under. Momentum stalled from there. He picked up six consecutive pars to make the turn in 34 strokes, two under for his day. Another birdied followed at the 10th before a rare blemish, a first bogey in 33 holes, coming at the 13th following a wayward iron shot. But Power recovered well, and birdied the 14th and 17th holes to get into the clubhouse at 16 under par.
